title: Measurement-induced entanglement phases in hyperbolic gauge-Higgs models
authors: Cole Kelson-Packer, Hiroki Sukeno, Akimasa Miyake
abstract: Gauge-Higgs theory in flat spacetime provides a prime theoretical model of multiple phases of matter with distinct entanglement structures. More recently, there has been interest in hyperbolic space and the influence its extensive boundaries have on these structures. Entanglement transitions between non-equilibrium phases, such as topological phases, can be realized by the competition of non-commutating measurements. Here we study the entanglement phases of gauge-Higgs models on hyperbolic lattices described by measurement-only dynamics. We chart 2D phase diagrams by employing topological entanglement entropy and introducing a generalized measurement-induced entanglement tailored for hyperbolic Higgs phases. Utilizing duality, we find a phase absent in Euclidean space, wherein the bulk lattice hosts separated clusters of symmetry-protected topological order. Transitions between this "archipelago" phase and neighboring topological and trivial phases feature a critical exponent $δ$ belonging to a mean-field universality class. Our essential tool is a 3D resource state inspired by measurement-based quantum computation that simulates the spacetime evolution of the 2D quantum state with a third direction of entanglement. This allows us to analyze spacetime "sponges" of entanglement, which map to classical percolation theory and allow us to infer values of critical points on our phase diagrams' boundaries.
summary: This paper analyzes entanglement phases in gauge-Higgs models on hyperbolic lattices using measurement-only dynamics. By simulating spacetime evolution via a 3D resource state, the authors map out 2D phase diagrams, predicting a unique 'archipelago' phase absent in flat space. This work provides a powerful link between quantum information theory and the study of topological order in strongly correlated systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the entanglement phases of gauge-Higgs models when placed on hyperbolic lattices, specifically focusing on entanglement transitions driven by non-commuting measurements.
main_result: The research predicts a novel 'archipelago' phase, absent in Euclidean space, where separated clusters of Symmetry-Protected Topological (SPT) order exist, and transitions into this phase follow a mean-field universality class.
method: The authors employ measurement-only dynamics (MOCs) simulated using a 3D resource state inspired by measurement-based quantum computation to chart 2D phase diagrams.
model_or_system: The system is a gauge-Higgs model defined on hyperbolic lattices, analyzed via measurement-only dynamics involving random circuits alternating between Z and X measurements.
key_observables: Topological entanglement entropy, generalized measurement-induced entanglement, Von Neumann entropy, and the detection of Wilson lines/loops to characterize topological order.
important_parameters: Measurement probabilities ($p_J, p_K$), lattice structure defined by Schläfli symbols $\{P, Q\}$, and critical exponents ($\delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a correspondence between $Z_2$ Euclidean lattice field theory path integrals and imaginary-time evolutions, and that entanglement entropies are independent of specific measurement outcomes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate idealized phase diagrams for both Euclidean and hyperbolic settings, showing the predicted intermediate 'archipelago' phase in the hyperbolic case, and diagrams detailing the foliated resource state construction.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the physical system (gauge-Higgs on hyperbolic lattices) to detailing the simulation method (3D resource state/MBQC), mapping observables (entropy, Wilson loops) to phases (trivial, topological, SPT), and finally presenting the key results regarding the unique hyperbolic phase diagram.
why_interesting: The work connects concepts from quantum information (MBQC, resource states) directly to condensed matter phenomena (topological order, phase transitions) in a non-trivial geometric setting (hyperbolic space), offering new tools for understanding entanglement structure.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Idealized phase diagrams of the Z2 Fradkin-Shenker model (left) [15, 19] and a gauge-Higgs measurement-only circuit (right) [20]. The bottom depicts the Hamiltonian and measurements considered in each respective model. The dashed lines indicate that a boundary transition separates the confined/trivial and Higgs/SPT phases. At the top center is a {4, 4} lattice with up to L = 2 layers and rough boundaries.

FIG. 2. Cartoon of a hyperbolic MOC. The idealized phase diagram (right) contains labels and depictions of each phase. A full intermediate phase replaces the critical line in Euclidean space. The left depicts a {5, 5} lattice with up to L = 1 layers and smooth boundaries, along with probabilistically measured stabilizers. Our diagnostics detect the boundary transition between SPT and trivial phases at the future temporal – rather than spatial – boundary. The spins in the bubbles representing different phases reflect the spatial correlation of measurement outcomes. Measurements in the trivial phase are uncorrelated, but positively correlated along loops and lines in the topological and SPT...

FIG. 3. Drawings of an MBQC resource cell for an MOC for N = {5, 5} (a) and a spacetime sponge (b). A P-gon replaces the top and bottom plaquettes of the cell for general {P, Q}. The full resource glues cells together such that a slice of the Z-timestep resembles {P, Q}. The spacetime sponge M is shown as an operator OM shaded red with labeled components XM, X∂M, and Zγ compatible with the measurement history {Pres}. To the right, from bottom to top, is a corresponding Wilson line’s simulated time evolution.

FIG. 4. Illustration of a Wilson loop operator contributing to Stop for the parties A, B, and C, shown in terms of the 2D simulated state (top) and 3D resource (bottom). Both edges and vertices are included in the A, B and C. In line with [22], we split an annulus in the lattice into quadrants, with two opposite regions given to A and C, and the remainder given to B = B1 ∪B2.

FIG. 6. Illustration of the ghost connectivity Ih(Q, r). We randomly entangle resource vertices with ghost qubits Q (cir- cled in green) and the fixed root r. The ghost connectivity Ih(Q, r) is nonzero if a sponge connects Q and r. The typi- cal behavior of Ih(Q, r) is depicted, showing how δ must be extracted from intermediate values of log(h) to avoid nonuni- versal and finite-size effects.
